answer.rationale: The two live deficits are activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ); the competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal but the weakest lever. memory_73 is the one inherited record that reports a full funnel: 40% SMB discount lifted signups +31% and revenue +18% while costing 12pp of monthly retention with the segment definition held constant. That is a top-line gain purchased with durable churn, which is directly counter to the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so promotional_pricing is rejected without spending verification on it. referral_incentive (memory_57) is sound but works on established customers and does nothing for the two metrics actually declining. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment not under pressure. That leaves simplify_onboarding and activation_messaging, both plausible; I choose simplify_onboarding because memory_86 targets completion and time-to-value directly, and it plausibly propagates upstream into the activation number, whereas messaging (memory_91) touches engagement only. I spend the budget on memory_86 (the record my action rests on) and memory_31 (the adjacent signup-simplification result), because both are summarized as clean causal wins with no retention, revenue-quality, or duration figures attached — exactly the shape memory_73 would have had if it were compressed to its headline. What I need from the archive is whether either measured downstream retention or qualified-revenue quality, and over what window; a 'durable lift in first-week activation' says nothing about month three. The specific downstream risk is that cutting signup and onboarding friction admits lower-intent accounts, inflating activation while quietly degrading cohort quality — the same failure mode as the discount, arriving through a different door. So I run this as a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue-per-cohort as blocking guardrails, not activation alone, and I hold the segment definition fixed so the comparison stays honest. Residual uncertainty: these memories are ~15-64 days stale, the market has since shifted, and the simultaneous activation and onboarding declines may share an unmeasured common cause (possibly the competitor drawing off high-intent traffic) that no onboarding change will fix. If verification shows memory_86 measured only completion with no retention follow-through, I would narrow to a small_guarded_test rather than proceed at standard scale.
